purpose: Hand-transcribed inputs for docs/evidence/sputter_yields_v1/build_sputter_yields_v1.py. Every number below was read by the lane from the cited page image (or, for atomic weights, from the cited web table) on the stated date. Nothing here is an alloy or coating value. The builder derives the register JSON and MD from this file only; it refuses missing or unknown fields.

decision.verbatim_quote: We can freeze those values now for the next rebuild as owner-defined screening guardbands: `E_screen = 1.10 × E_threshold` and `F_worst = 1.25`. Regenerate the sputter register from the unchanged source data after this decision. These are screening/down-selection factors only, not P4 material-acceptance, lifetime, or qualification thresholds; those remain governed by the pre-exposure P4 rule already established in S5.12. No later adjustment merely because a material passes or fails.

use_in_this_register.E_screen_factor: E_screen = E_screen_factor x E_threshold (the printed APID fit Eth): TRIM.SP points with E < E_screen are reported but excluded from the APID-reproduction screen (CHK-APID-REPRODUCTION)
use_in_this_register.F_worst: screen tolerance: the worst fit/TRIM.SP factor max(r, 1/r) over the points with E >= E_screen must be <= F_worst, otherwise the build fails as a transcription / formula-reading error

screening_guardbands.scope: SCREENING / DOWN-SELECTION ONLY. Never a P4 material-acceptance, lifetime, erosion or qualification threshold; those are frozen at LOCK-2 after metrology commissioning, before exposure (S5.12, A9.12 P4-OQ-03). In this register no material passes or fails on these factors.
screening_guardbands.provenance_history: The first build carrying these factors (commit 1d595ad, SPUTTER-1 repair) used the same values as lane-chosen builder constants (APID_NEAR_THRESHOLD = 1.1, APID_REPRO_TOL_FACTOR = 1.25) selected AFTER the lane had seen the TRIM.SP / APID data. That build's screening results are therefore NOT pre-registered evidence and are not represented as such. A9.17 freezes the values as owner constants; this regeneration applies them prospectively to the unchanged source data. No value was adjusted after seeing whether any row or material passes.

screening_outcomes.note: copied from the first-build register (register_json_sha256 above): apid_fits_transcribed and CHK-APID-REPRODUCTION; used only for the regenerated-vs-first-build comparison, never to change a factor

applied: P4-OQ-04 / S5.13 answer BOTH: lawful acquisition of species-resolved N+, N2+, O+, O2+ sputtering-yield information (library, inter-library loan, publisher purchase, institutional subscription, other licensed routes) plus project ion-beam measurement of down-selected candidates; literature is used for prior bounds, test-matrix selection, comparison and model initialisation; project measurements provide candidate-specific evidence; elemental-target literature yields are never silently substituted for an alloy/coating.

P4-OQ-02 / S5.11 answer BROAD_Q0_DOWNSELECT_Q1: the Q0 matrix rows used in q0_matrix below; coatings must record composition, thickness, deposition process, substrate, surface preparation and lot/process provenance; Ti, TiN/ZrN, bulk Cu and bulk Ir are reserve only (not in this register's matrix).
P4-OQ-03 / S5.12 answer LOCK_2_AFTER_METROLOGY_BEFORE_EXPOSURE: sputter/erosion acceptance thresholds are frozen at LOCK-2 after metrology commissioning; this register sets no threshold.

sources.access_detail: MPG PuRe open repository; scanned report with OCR text layer; every value used was read from the rendered page image (OCR is noisy)
sources.kind: TRIM.SP binary-collision Monte Carlo tables (calculated, not measured)
sources.scope_note: index (report pp. 5-6): among the Q0-relevant elements only C, Fe, Ni, Mo (not in Q0 as bulk), Ti, Pt, W are targets; N projectiles only on Be, C (15-30 keV only, out of range) and W; O projectiles only on Be, B, C, Mo, W and compounds (BeO, B4C, B2O3, B(OH)3, WO3, WO4, layered WO3 on W). The report states the values are valid for nearly flat surfaces; statistical errors usually < 3 % for yields > 1e-5, up to 100 % at the lowest values; several O tables are flagged 'only low fluence!' (no oxide / compound build-up).

nifs_worked_example.note: the printed example mixes 195.1 and 197 for the Au mass and prints gamma = 0.07878 (our arithmetic with its own masses gives 0.0781); the builder accepts a 2 % tolerance on the yield and records the residual

nifs_formula_reading.alpha_branch_note: Eq. (17) as printed labels 0.249(M2/M1)^0.56 + 0.0035(M2/M1)^1.5 'M1 >= M2' and 0.088(M2/M1)^-0.15 + 0.165(M2/M1) 'M1 <= M2'. The paper's own worked example (He -> Au, M2/M1 = 48.75, i.e. M1 < M2) and Fig. 1 use the 0.249 branch for M2/M1 > 1, so the labels as printed are inconsistent with the paper's use. The builder uses the branch the paper itself uses (0.249 branch for M1 <= M2); the two branches agree at M2/M1 = 1 (0.2525 vs 0.253). Only O+ / N+ on C (M1 > M2) is affected.
nifs_formula_reading.threshold_note: Eq. (18): Eth/Us = 6.7/gamma for M1 >= M2 and (1 + 5.7 M1/M2)/gamma for M1 <= M2 (labels consistent with the worked example).
